findings.title: Upsampling eligibility uses the outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset
findings.body: _get_event_stats receives scoped_dataset, which can differ from the closure dataset during dashboard discover-split handling (e.g. an errors-only call is made with discover while the outer dataset is metrics/discover, or vice versa). is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects is nevertheless passed the outer dataset, so eligibility is decided for the wrong dataset: error split results can miss upsampling and transaction/metrics split results can be decided from the wrong dataset context. Pass scoped_dataset to the eligibility check.

findings.title: Substring check treats negated and mixed-type queries as error-only
findings.body: _is_error_focused_query returns True whenever the raw query contains the substring 'event.type:error', including '!event.type:error' (which excludes errors) and mixed queries such as 'event.type:transaction OR event.type:error'. In those cases count() is replaced by sum(sample_weight), a column that is not meaningful for transactions/default events, so results will be wrong or undercounted. The check needs to use the parsed search query and only apply when the query provably restricts to error events.

findings.title: Error-focus detection reads request.GET instead of the actual query being executed
findings.body: _is_error_focused_query ignores the query argument passed through _get_event_stats and only inspects request.GET['query']. Callers that synthesize or modify the query (for example the dashboard split path builds '(query) AND !event.type:transaction' for the errors-only probe) therefore get eligibility decided from a different query than the one sent to Snuba, so genuinely error-only split queries are not upsampled unless the original GET parameter happens to contain 'event.type:error'. Pass the effective query string into the eligibility decision.

findings.title: upsampled_count is enabled for the errors dataset but only registered on Discover
findings.body: _should_apply_sample_weight_transform always returns True for the errors dataset, causing count() to be rewritten to 'upsampled_count() as count', but the new SnQLFunction is only added to DiscoverDatasetConfig.function_converter in discover.py; the errors dataset config is untouched. A request with dataset=errors on an allowlisted project will therefore send an unregistered function to the errors query builder and fail validation instead of returning stats. Register upsampled_count for the errors dataset (and any other dataset for which the transform is enabled) or restrict the transform to datasets that define it; the added Snuba tests never exercise dataset=errors.

findings.title: sum(sample_weight) drops events that have no sample weight
findings.body: The upsampled_count aggregate is a bare sum(sample_weight) wrapped in toInt64. Events in allowlisted projects that were ingested without error sampling (or before sample_weight was populated) have a NULL/0 sample_weight, so they contribute nothing and can make an entire bucket NULL/0 instead of counting once, silently under-reporting historical and unsampled errors. The aggregate should treat a missing weight as 1 (e.g. sum(coalesce/ifNull(sample_weight, 1))) so unsampled events count normally.

findings.title: Stray nested-repository pointer file committed
findings.body: This adds a top-level file named 'sentry-repo' whose entire content is 'Subproject commit a5d2909...', i.e. an accidental gitlink/submodule artifact without any .gitmodules entry. It is unrelated to the upsampling feature, pollutes the repository root, and can confuse tooling that scans the tree. Remove the file before merging.
